In algebraic geometry, the '''<math>\lambda_g</math>-conjecture''' gives a particularly simple formula for certain integrals on the Deligne–Mumford compactification <math>\overline{\mathcal M}_{g, n}</math> of the [[moduli space of curves]] with marked points. It was first found as a consequence of the [[Virasoro conjecture]] by {{harvs|txt|first=E. |last=Getzler |author-link=Ezra Getzler |first2=R. |last2=Pandharipande | author2-link=Rahul Pandharipande |arxiv=math.AG/9805114 |title=Virasoro constraints and the Chern classes of the Hodge bundle|journal=Nuclear Physics B |volume=530 |issue=3|pages=701–714 |year=1998 }}. Later, it was proven by {{harvs|txt | first=C. |last=Faber |first2=R. |last2=Pandharipande |author2-link=Rahul Pandharipande |arxiv=math.AG/9805114 |title=Hodge integrals, partition matrices, and the <math>\lambda_g</math> conjecture|journal=Ann. of Math. |series= 2|volume=157 |issue=1|pages=97–124 |year=2003 }} using virtual localization in [[Gromov–Witten theory]]. It is named after the factor of <math>\lambda_g</math>, the ''g''th [[Chern class]] of the [[Hodge bundle]], appearing in its integrand. The other factor is a monomial in the <math>\psi_i</math>, the first Chern classes of the ''n'' cotangent line bundles, as in [[Witten's conjecture]].

Let <math>a_1, \ldots, a_n</math> be positive integers such that:

:<math>a_1 + \cdots + a_n = 2g-3+n.</math>

Then the <math>\lambda_g</math>-formula can be stated as follows:

: <math>\int_{\overline{\mathcal M}_{g, n}} \psi_1^{a_1} \cdots \psi_n^{a_n}\lambda_g = \binom{2g + n - 3}{a_1, \ldots, a_n} \int_{\overline{\mathcal M}_{g, 1}} \psi_1^{2g - 2}\lambda_g.</math>

The <math>\lambda_g</math>-formula in combination with

:<math>\int_{\overline{\mathcal M}_{g, 1}} \psi_1^{2g - 2}\lambda_g = \frac{2^{2g-1} - 1}{2^{2g - 1}} \frac{|B_{2g}|}{(2g)!},</math>

where the ''B''<sub>2''g''</sub> are [[Bernoulli number]]s, gives a way to calculate all integrals on <math>\overline{\mathcal M}_{g, n}</math> involving products in <math>\psi</math>-classes and a factor of <math>\lambda_g</math>.
